questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests per-namespace scoping, ConfigMap-driven config, and a small policy engine. Exercises InitContainers, Secrets, PVC logging, and network boundaries.

## Key Concepts
- Per-namespace Deployment
- ConfigMap-driven configuration
- Lightweight policy checks (privilege, caps, readOnlyRootFilesystem)
- InitContainer with jq/curl
- Secret-based tokens and PVC-backed logs
- Namespace NetworkPolicy scope

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: namespace-scanner
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: namespace-scanner
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: namespace-scanner
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-progress curl jq"]
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      containers:
      - name: scanner
        image: myrepo/namespace-scanner:latest
        env:
        - name: PORTAL_URL
          value: "https://compliance-portal/api/v1/scan"
        - name: TOKEN
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: compliance-portal-token
              key: token
        volumeMounts:
        - name: logs
          mountPath: /logs
      volumes:
      - name: logs
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: compliance-logs
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this policy in CI?
- How would you handle retries and idempotence when posting digests?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests secret handling, TLS/mTLS basics, mounting certs, and correct network isolation for a real-world integration.

## Key Concepts
- Secrets and volume mounts
- TLS/Certificates and mTLS basics
- NetworkPolicy egress controls
- Rollout and secret rotation strategies

## Code Example
```javascript
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: tls-secret
type: Opaque
data:
  tls.crt: <base64>
  tls.key: <base64>
  ca.crt: <base64>
```

```javascript
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payments-api
  namespace: prod
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: payments
        image: payments-api:latest
        env:
        - name: TLS_PATH
          value: /certs
        volumeMounts:
        - name: tls
          mountPath: /certs
      volumes:
      - name: tls
        secret:
          secretName: tls-secret
```

```javascript
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: payments-egress
  namespace: prod
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payments-api
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 203.0.113.45/32
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

> Note: DNS-based egress restrictions are not widely supported in NetworkPolicy; use the processor’s IP in the ipBlock.

Why This Is Asked

Gives candidates a concrete task focusing on PodSecurity basics, not just data pipelines. It combines ConfigMap/Secret usage, a simple audit logic, and a secure, isolated network path.

## Key Concepts

- Deployment scope per namespace
- InitContainer installation of tooling
- ConfigMap-driven rules
- Secret-based credentials
- HTTP POST of results
- TLS cert rotation sidecar
- NetworkPolicy egress scoping
- Readiness/liveness probes

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: namespace-security-audit
  namespace: <namespace>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: namespace-security-audit
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: namespace-security-audit
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq yq && echo ready"]
      containers:
        - name: audit-agent
          image: myrepo/audit-agent:latest
          env:
            - name: AUDIT_CONFIG_MAP
              value: audit-config
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: audit-portal-credentials
      volumes:
        - name: audit-scripts
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: audit-pvc
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you simulate/verify audit-portal responses in CI?
- How would you adjust for namespace churn (new namespaces)?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: multi-container pod design, InitContainers, PVCs, ConfigMaps, Secrets, TLS sidecars, probes, PDBs, and network policies, plus load validation and rollback strategies.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer for tooling setup
- PVC mounting and data direction between /data/events and /data/enriched
- ConfigMap/Secret for runtime config and credentials
- TLS sidecar for certificate rotation
- Readiness and Liveness probes
- PodDisruptionBudget
- NetworkPolicy for scoped egress
- Load testing and rollback workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator-config
data:
  batchSize: "100"
  enrichmentEndpoint: "http://enrich-controller.analytics.svc.cluster.local:8080/enrich"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator-creds
type: Opaque
data:
  apiToken: <base64-encoded-token>
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: config-aggregator
  namespace: analytics
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: config-aggregator
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: config-aggregator
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: init-tools
          image: alpine:3.17
          command: ["sh","-c","apk add --no-cache curl jq; sleep 0"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /data
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: myrepo/config-aggregator:latest
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: config-aggregator-config
            - secretRef:
                name: config-aggregator-creds
          volumeMounts:
            - name: events
              mountPath: /data/events
            - name: enriched
              mountPath: /data/enriched
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /healthz
              port: 9000
            initialDelaySeconds: 10
            periodSeconds: 5
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /readyz
              port: 9000
            initialDelaySeconds: 20
            periodSeconds: 10
      volumes:
        - name: events
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: config-aggregator-events-pvc
        - name: enriched
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: config-aggregator-enriched-pvc
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt this for namespace isolation across multiple environments?
- What scaling considerations arise with batchSize tuning and backpressure?
- How would you observe and debug under intermittent enrichment endpoint failures?

## Key Concepts
- Namespace-scoped RBAC auditing via in-cluster commands

apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: rbac-audit
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      serviceAccountName: restricted-sa
      initContainers:
      - name: install-tools
        image: alpine:3.18
        command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache kubectl curl jq"]

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD mastery: per-namespace isolation, InitContainer usage, secret/config management, and production-grade guarantees.

## Key Concepts
- InitContainer for model pull from Secret
- ConfigMap and Secret usage for runtime parameters
- Probes and HPA for reliability and scale
- Idempotent DB writes to achieve at-least-once delivery
- NetworkPolicy to enforce namespace boundaries

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ns-image-resize
  namespace: <ns>
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: image-resize
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: fetch-model
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "download-model.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: model
              mountPath: /models
      containers:
        - name: processor
          image: registry/ns-image-resize:latest
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8080
          envFrom:
            - secretRef: { name: resize-secret }
      volumes:
        - name: model
          emptyDir: {}
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 15
        periodSeconds: 20
      affinity:
        podAntiAffinity:
          preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            - weight: 100
              podAffinityTerm:
                labelSelector:
                  matchLabels:
                    app: image-resize
                topologyKey: "kubernetes.io/hostname"
  ```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor idempotency and retry behavior?
- What changes if Kafka offset management moves to a separate transactional store?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Security hardening of container runtimes and correctness of patching deployments are critical in real-world CKAD tasks.

## Key Concepts
- SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities drop
- Probes: readiness and liveness on /healthz
- Deployment strategy: RollingUpdate for zero-downtime upgrades
- Validation: load testing, rollout status, and rollback workflow

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: portal
  namespace: secure-app
spec:
  replicas: 2
  strategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      maxUnavailable: 0
      maxSurge: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: portal
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: portal
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nginx
        image: nginx:1.25
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          capabilities:
            drop:
            - ALL
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 2
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 80
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
          timeoutSeconds: 2
``` 

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adjust if the app requires a limited capability set?
- How would you implement canary rollouts and monitor for regression?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD abilities: scheduling with CronJob, cross-resource coordination (ConfigMap/Secret), PVC usage, InitContainer setup, and NetworkPolicy scoping. It emphasizes per-namespace isolation and minimal instrumentation for reliability.

## Key Concepts
- CronJob per-namespace scheduling
- ConfigMap/Secret usage for config and credentials
- InitContainer provisioning of benchmarking tools
- Logs to PVC and metrics to ConfigMap
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for restricted egress

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1beta1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: bench-endpoint
  namespace: {NAMESPACE}
spec:
  schedule: "*/15 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
            - name: install-tools
              image: alpine:3.18
              command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache wrk && sleep 1"]
          containers:
            - name: bench
              image: appropriate/curl
              command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "wrk -t2 -c50 -d30s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $BENCH_TOKEN\" $BENCH_ENDPOINT || true"]
              envFrom:
                - configMapRef:
                    name: bench-config
              env:
                - name: BENCH_ENDPOINT
                  valueFrom:
                    configMapKeyRef:
                      name: bench-config
                      key: endpoint
                - name: BENCH_TOKEN
                  valueFrom:
                    secretKeyRef:
                      name: bench-secret
                      key: token
              volumeMounts:
                - name: logs
                  mountPath: /logs
          volumes:
            - name: logs
              persistentVolumeClaim:
                claimName: bench-logs
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle token rotation without restarting all CronJobs?
- How would you scale probes and tolerations to handle namespace density?

```yaml
  namespace: example-ns
spec:
  schedule: "*/10 * * * *"
  successfulJobsHistoryLimit: 3
  failedJobsHistoryLimit: 1
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: tools-installer
            image: busybox:1.36
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              wget -q https://github.com/stedolan/jq/releases/download/jq-1.6/jq-linux64 -O /tmp/jq
              chmod +x /tmp/jq
              apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tmp
          containers:
          - name: scanner
            image: trivy-lite:latest
            volumeMounts:
            - name: manifests
              mountPath: /manifests
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /tools
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              export PATH=/tmp:$PATH
              for manifest in /manifests/*.yaml; do
                trivy scan --format json -o /logs/$(basename $manifest).json $manifest
              done
              kubectl get configmap security-scan -n example-ns -o yaml > /logs/configmap-backup.yaml
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - ls
                - /logs
              initialDelaySeconds: 5
              periodSeconds: 10
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - cat
                - /tmp/health
              initialDelaySeconds: 15
              periodSeconds: 20
          volumes:
          - name: manifests
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: manifest-pvc
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: log-pvc
          - name: tools
            emptyDir: {}
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Trade-offs
- **PVC vs ConfigMap**: Using a PVC for logs allows for larger log volumes and retention, but requires storage provisioning. ConfigMaps are simpler but size-limited.
- **InitContainer vs Sidecar**: InitContainers run once per pod startup; sidecars run continuously. For a CronJob, InitContainers are more cost-effective.
- **NetworkPolicy**: Restricting egress improves security but may break updates if registries change. Consider using DNS whitelisting rather than specific IP ranges.
- **Probe timing**: Aggressive probes may cause premature failures; conservative settings increase job execution time.
- **CronJob frequency**: More frequent scans catch vulnerabilities faster but increase cluster load and API calls.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of the sidecar pattern for config reloading without full pod restarts.

## Key Concepts
- Sidecar container pattern
- inotify for file system monitoring
- SIGHUP for process signal handling
- ConfigMap mounting and reload behavior
- Zero-downtime configuration updates

## Patch Example
```yaml
# payments/processor-deployment.yaml
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: config-watcher
          image: busybox:stable
          command:
            - /bin/sh
            - -c
            - |
              apk add --no-cache inotify-tools
              inotifywait -m -e modify -r /etc/processor |
              while read path event; do
                kill -HUP 1
              done
          securityContext:
            runAsNonRoot: true
            runAsUser: 65534
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/processor
              readOnly: true
```

## Verification Under Load
1. Apply patch and verify pod rollout: `kubectl rollout status deployment/processor -n payments`
2. Simulate ConfigMap update: `kubectl create configmap processor-config --from-literal=data=updated --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`
3. Verify sidecar detects change: `kubectl logs processor-<pod> -c config-watcher -n payments`
4. Confirm main process reloads: check application logs for reload indicators
5. Load test with tools like `hey` or `wrk` to verify zero downtime during reload

## Rollback Procedure
1. `kubectl rollout undo deployment/processor -n payments`
2. Verify previous version: `kubectl rollout status deployment/processor -n payments`
3. Confirm stable state: `kubectl get pods -n payments -l app=processor`

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: PVCs, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, sidecars, readiness/liveness, and network policies in a realistic static content scenario.

Key Concepts
- PVC-backed volumes and ConfigMap mounts
- InitContainer for initial bootstrap
- Sidecar for live file reloads
- ConfigMap-driven content flags
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: static-content-server
  namespace: ckad-demo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: static-content
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: static-content
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: html
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: static-content-pvc
        - name: template
          configMap:
            name: page-template
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: page-config
      initContainers:
        - name: init
          image: alpine
          command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /template/index.html /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: html
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
            - name: template
              mountPath: /template
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:alpine
          volumeMounts:
            - name: html
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
        - name: reload-agent
          image: busybox
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do inotifywait -e modify /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html; nginx -s reload; done"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: html
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /index.html
          port: 80
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /index.html
          port: 80
        initialDelaySeconds: 15
        periodSeconds: 20
```

Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle multi-namespace isolation if the same config is needed across namespaces?
- What changes if you switch to an A/B testing banner using two ConfigMaps and a canary rollout?

```javascript
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:

spec:

      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: compliance
            image: registry.example/compliance:latest
            env:

              value: "https://cve-feed.local/api/v1/checks"

```
